Hi, I\'m unibot, the assistant that lives on your phone. Let me take a few things off your plate.

A bit about how I work:

- I have my own computer — a Linux sandbox and a browser — so I can run commands, open websites and fill in forms.
- I can read and organise the files and photos you mount for me, and take care of reminders and scheduled tasks.
- Before any step that matters, I ask you first.
- Everything runs on this phone; your messages go only to the model you configured.

These files are the agent\'s: who it is, what it knows about you, what it remembers, what it writes for you and when it wakes up. They live in your phone\'s storage — the agent reads and edits them from its shell under /var/minis/memory, and you can edit anything here.

This is the agent\'s persona: the values and habits it tries to hold to in every conversation, its name, and the style it answers in. It starts from a template that ships with unibot; the agent may refine it over time and tells you when it does. You can edit it at any time. This note is not part of the file.

The agent keeps this file as its working notes about you: your name, how you like to be addressed, your timezone, and the context it needs to be useful, such as what you are working on. It fills it in over time from your conversations and reads it at the start of each one. It reflects the agent\'s current understanding, so it can be incomplete or out of date. You can edit anything here, and the agent will follow what you write. This note is not part of the file.

Durable notes the agent keeps across conversations — the things worth remembering, in its own words, plus anything you imported from another assistant. The day-by-day diary lives beside it in the memory folder. Read at the start of every conversation when memory is on. This note is not part of the file.
One paragraph that steers the feed: what you want more of, what to skip, how long posts should be. The daily feed routine reads it before writing. This note is not part of the file.

When the agent wakes up on its own: every routine and every goal check, with its schedule and how the last run went. Rendered from the routines, so it is read-only here — change them from Goals → Routines. This note is not part of the file.
Write %1$s in Markdown. Headings and bullet points read best; keep secrets out.
Nothing here yet. Tap the pencil to write it, or let the agent fill it in as you talk.
What runs on its own, and when. Rendered from the routines; edit them from Goals → Routines.

Bring over what another assistant already knows about you. Ask it with the prompt below, paste its answer here, and it is appended to GLOBAL.md under “Imported” — where your agent reads it at the start of every conversation.

Please gather everything you remember about me into a concise list of bullet points: who I am, how I like to be addressed, where I live and my timezone, what I do, what I am working on right now, my preferences and habits, and anything you were told to always or never do. Plain text, no headings, no secrets or passwords.
Look it over first: leave out passwords, card numbers and anything you would not want in a plain text file on your phone.

Three models, each chosen on its own: the chat model you talk to, an image model for the avatar and pictures, a video model that makes the avatar move. One Alibaba Cloud Model Studio key covers all three.
The default model group. Every conversation, the feed and the daily routines run on it.

Avatar changes, the four candidates and the poses, and any picture you ask for in the chat. The list is what your provider reports for this key, filtered to models that draw. Alibaba Cloud Model Studio: qwen-image-3.0 (draws and poses; ¥0.18 a picture) or the Pro tier. OpenAI: gpt-image-1. Any provider with the OpenAI images endpoint works.
None of your providers can draw. Add an OpenAI-compatible provider (Alibaba Cloud Model Studio, OpenAI, xAI, OpenRouter or a custom base URL) with an API key; the avatar is drawn with your own key.
Until one is set, the avatar cannot be changed and no pictures can be drawn. The agent will say so if you ask.

Makes the avatar move — a short looping clip for each state — and any clip you ask for. Alibaba Cloud Model Studio: wan2.2-i2v-flash (recommended, ¥0.10 a second at 480P), another Wan model or MiniMax/MiniMax-H3; the list shows the ones this key can use, each activated once on the model\'s card in the Model Studio console. Billed per second of video; an avatar takes four clips of a few seconds.

No provider that can make video yet — unibot speaks Alibaba Cloud Model Studio\'s video API, which unibot Cloud relays too. Sign in to unibot Cloud, or add a Model Studio key (it can be the same one as the image model uses), and the avatar starts moving; until then it stays as still pictures.
Optional. Without one, the avatar stays still and no clips can be made.

unibot is free and open source, and needs no account: paste an API key from any provider and start talking. Your key and your words go straight to the provider you chose — nothing passes through unibot servers, because there are none.
With two permissions it can open apps, tap and type for you. A capsule with each step and a Stop button stays on screen; logins, passwords and codes are always yours.
Everything else works without these. They live under Settings → Hands whenever you want them.
Before anything it cannot take back — deleting, sending, paying — it stops and asks you first.

When the agent needs your yes while the app is in the background — a routine at 3 a.m. wanting to delete something — a notification with Allow and Deny buttons appears. The decision resumes the agent immediately; the app does not need to be open. Standing grants are only ever given from the in-chat approval card, never from a notification.
Keep chats in sync across your devices
Derives the encryption key for sync snapshots (PBKDF2, 120,000 rounds). It is never stored and never leaves this phone — you will enter it again after the app restarts.
Sign in to unibot Cloud first — sync rides on the cloud relay connection.

The cloud relay does not offer a session-sync endpoint yet (its API covers chat, the agent profile, sign-in sessions and the activity log). Snapshots are encrypted on this phone and held ready — nothing is uploaded. The payloads are already end-to-end encrypted, so when the relay grows a sync endpoint it will only ever see ciphertext.
Snapshot ready: %1$d sessions encrypted on this phone.

Nothing is uploaded. The file is made on this phone and handed to the Android share sheet — you choose where it goes, every single time.
A catalog is only fetched when you tap Load — never automatically. It must be a JSON file in the bundled catalog\'s format.

Adds an MCP server to this phone. It appears under Settings → MCP, where you can enable it per chat.
